The prevailing wisdom in text-to-image (T2I) generation

ter performance.
This “bigger is better” paradigm has
driven the field to billion-scale image-text paired datasets

essary to capture the full text-image distribution, in this
work, we challenge this assumption and argue that data

and quality in model training.

**Title**: How far can we go with ImageNet for Text-to-Image generation?  
**Abstract**: Recent text-to-image (T2I) generation models have achieved remarkable results by training on billion-scale datasets, following a 'bigger is better' paradigm. We challenge this by demonstrating that strategic data augmentation of small, well-curated datasets can match or outperform models trained on massive web-scraped datasets. Using only ImageNet enhanced with well-designed text and image augmentations, we achieve a +2 overall score over SD-XL on GenEval and +5 on DPGBench while using just 1/10th the parameters and 1/1000th the training images.
